justification: Real logic change to the DCP review-queue fidelity checker (scripts/dcp_fidelity_gate.py) plus a scoping change to what it grades at all, and one small behavioural change to how rows are inserted (scripts/dcp_extract_changed.py). Standard rather than Light because it changes what gets written to dcp_review_queue.fidelity_status/status for every pending row across all 9 councils, and a wrong exclusion could silently hide a genuine hallucinated number. Standard rather than Critical because nothing here touches the served table (regulatory_provisions) or auto-approves anything into production -- dcp_review_queue is a human-gated staging table, the exclusions and scoping only affect which rows a human sees as 'needs review' vs 'grounded' vs 'not yet relevant', numeric changes always still require a human unless the number is demonstrably present in the source text, and every exclusion pattern and the scoping definition were verified against real flagged rows and the project's own established 'live+actionable' definition (not invented) before being added.

real_layer_exempt.scripts/dcp_extract_changed.py: enqueue_review_changes's INSERT into dcp_review_queue (table, columns, placeholder count) is byte-for-byte unchanged by this branch -- the only change is which pure-Python value (row_status, computed from the new auto_reject boolean) gets passed as one of the existing parameters. That computation has no DB/HTTP surface of its own and is already covered by tests/test_dcp_extraction_fidelity.py::TestRowLevelFailurePreRejected (test_status_is_derived_from_fidelity_not_hardcoded, test_auto_reject_reasons_exclude_the_two_size_heuristics, test_near_certain_reasons_still_auto_reject). Real-DB-style coverage for what actually IS new in this branch (the chapters_query scoping SQL) lives in tests/test_dcp_fidelity_gate_real_db.py; a second real-DB test wrapping this file's unchanged INSERT would not verify anything the unit tests above don't already.
This IS the real-layer check, not a wrapper needing one: .claude/dq_checks.json's DQ-98 entry runs this exact script directly against production via scripts/dq_check.py on every DQ-ledger invocation -- a parallel pytest that re-imports run() and re-executes the same query a second way would test nothing a fresh dq_check.py run doesn't already. Already executed against the real production DB this session (not merely written): 7 active chapters measured over the 30MB threshold, largest canterbury_bankstown/chapter-7-6-belmore-and-lakemba at 139,006,750 bytes -- see the DQ-98 entries in .claude/dq_checks.json and .claude/DATA_QUALITY_TRACKER.md for the full corroborating evidence and root cause.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_dcp_fidelity_gate.py tests/test_dcp_extraction_fidelity.py -v; python scripts/dq_check.py; python scripts/dq_probe_oversized_pdf_oom_risk.py
falsifiable_check.fails_when: a genuine wrong number stops being flagged, a citation/heading exclusion swallows a real measurement, the page window stops widening correctly, a row-level 'failed' verdict stops auto-rejecting, a non-actionable row gets graded/counted when it shouldn't, a live+actionable chapter gets silently skipped, or the DQ ledger's two files (dq_checks.json / DATA_QUALITY_TRACKER.md) disagree
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Every exclusion has a paired negative test proving it does NOT fire on plain measurement prose, and every widening has a paired test proving a genuinely wrong/unrelated number still flags. TWO real regressions were caught this way, not just theorised: (1) sentence-level source verification (built to close a Sol HIGH masking finding) was shipped, re-run against real production data, and found to cause a SEVERE regression -- ashfield/blacktown/georges_river/hornsby jumped from single-digit flagged counts to 15-50%+ -- because real DCP PDFs are full of structural extraction messiness (unpunctuated tables, two-column-interleaved text) that naive sentence-splitting cannot handle; the mechanism was removed entirely rather than shipped half-working, and a regression test locks the length-guard variant of this in. (2) exact-phrase citation verification (the first fix for the same Sol finding) was ALSO found live to regress ashfield 3->23 flagged, because real PDF running headers repeat with different line-wrapping/whitespace across pages -- fixed by switching to word-by-word + digit verification (test_wrong_heading_not_blanked / test_hallucinated_clause_citation_not_blanked prove it still catches a genuinely wrong heading/citation). 62/62 fidelity tests pass (tests/test_dcp_fidelity_gate.py + tests/test_dcp_extraction_fidelity.py, re-verified 2026-09-07 after the chapters_query refactor); tests/test_dcp_fidelity_gate_real_db.py's 4 tests pass against the real production DB (PYTEST_REAL_DB=1) and are correctly deselected (0 selected, 4 deselected) in a normal run; full suite green, re-run rather than quoted here per this project's own stale-count rule.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_review_queue holds 5,660 pending rows across 9 councils. Before this branch: 597 flagged, 5,063 grounded (unscoped). After the false-positive fixes alone (no scoping yet): ~169-187 flagged, still against the full 5,660. After ALSO adding chapter+row scoping to what the project's own CLAUDE.md Database Quick Reference table defines as 'live + actionable (the served set)' (is_current AND v2_is_actionable) plus row-level non-actionable filtering (reusing enrichment/extractors/actionable_classifier.py, the project's existing extraction-time classifier): the TRUE relevant set is 2,662 rows, not 5,660 -- 53% of pending rows were sitting in chapters awaiting their first-ever approval, pure reference documents with zero live content, or are administrative/intro/definitions text that was never going to become served regulatory data even once approved. Final measured result against the correct, scoped denominator: 245 flagged of 2,662 (9.2%), verified live via direct DB query, not estimated.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Two, both caught by re-verifying against real data rather than trusting the design on paper. First: assumed exact-phrase and then sentence-level matching would be STRICTLY more precise than the original whole-window substring check. Both were shipped, both were re-run against real production rows, and both caused real regressions for the reasons above -- precision on a synthetic adversarial scenario does not imply precision on real, messy PDF extraction output. Second: assumed 'grade every pending row' was the right default scope. Directly challenged mid-session ('why am I reviewing these... only deal with provisions being served and in scope') -- checking live data confirmed over half of pending rows were never going to matter (backlog chapters awaiting first approval, pure reference guides, or administrative text), and the fidelity gate now defaults to skipping them rather than spending real R2/CPU grading content nobody will see.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new surface. dcp_fidelity_gate.py's confident-page/whole-chapter grounding design already existed -- this fix widens what 'the source' means for a confident match (a page window instead of one page, now proven necessary but bounded after two reverted over-corrections) and adds scoping using the project's OWN pre-existing 'live+actionable' definition and OWN pre-existing actionable-classifier, not a new one. The auto-reject change reuses the existing 'rejected' status value and the existing rejected+content-hash commit-blocking logic verbatim. DQ-98 (a separate, real production OOM finding surfaced while investigating why 3 ku_ring_gai chapters could not be graded) is registered with a probe reusing the existing dcp_chapter_registry.url_content_length column (already populated by the existing monitor) -- no new size-tracking mechanism, no fix attempted, explicitly scoped as follow-up work per user direction.

functions.name: ground_row
functions.input: a row's extracted text, its ref_number, and the chapter's {page_num: text} dict
functions.output: dict(status, detail, verified_page, source_quote) -- 'grounded' or 'flagged' with the reason
functions.why_it_changed: the source text it grounds against now widens to a page window (anchor +-1 for words, anchor+caption-pages only for numbers) instead of a single anchor page, and the number set it checks now excludes citation/caption/heading/footer numbers verified (word-by-word, not exact-phrase) against the whole chapter
functions.if_none: without the window widening, any provision whose real content spans a page break or a multi-page stitched table falsely fails the word-match threshold; without the citation exclusions, a table caption's own page number, a cross-reference, or a property street number gets treated as an unverified regulatory value and the row is wrongly sent to human review even though its content is entirely correct

functions.name: gate_chapter
functions.input: a council/chapter_key and its R2 PDF path
functions.output: (grounded, flagged, skipped_not_actionable) counts; writes fidelity_status only for graded rows
functions.why_it_changed: now classifies each row via the existing actionable_classifier before grading it -- an introduction/definitions/boilerplate row is skipped entirely (fidelity_status left untouched, never flagged, never counted as needing review) rather than spending a real PDF-comparison on content that could never become served regulatory data
functions.if_none: administrative rows keep consuming grading time and, if they happen to fail the word/number check for unrelated reasons, keep landing in front of a human reviewer for content that was never going to matter

functions.name: chapters_query
functions.input: council, an optional chapter_key filter, and the include_backlog bool from --include-backlog
functions.output: (sql, params) -- pulled out of main() so tests/test_dcp_fidelity_gate_real_db.py can execute the exact production query against the real database instead of a hand-copied approximation of it
functions.why_it_changed: new function -- pure refactor extracting main()'s existing inline chapter-selection SQL string-building with identical SQL/params (no behaviour change to main()), specifically to make the new EXISTS(...regulatory_provisions...is_current...v2_is_actionable...) scoping clause independently testable against real data, not just against a mock cursor
functions.if_none: the live+actionable scoping clause would only ever be verified by unit tests against a MagicMock cursor, which can prove the Python calling code handles whatever rows it's handed but can never prove the SQL itself selects the right chapters -- exactly the gap tests/test_dcp_fidelity_gate_real_db.py closes (verified live 2026-09-07: blacktown/part-a-car-parking correctly excluded by default and included with --include-backlog; ashfield/chapter-d-precinct-guidelines correctly included by default)

break_it.scenario: A genuinely wrong/hallucinated number happens to be immediately preceded by 'page'/'Figure'/'DS'/'PC'/'no.'/'p N-' in the same row's text, or shares a digit-string with a 'Figures N-M' range cited elsewhere in the same row.
break_it.what_happens: The exclusion is set-based per row, not proximity-aware, so the wrong number would be wrongly exempted from the numeric check and the row would ground when it should flag.
break_it.mitigated: Partially -- accepted, documented residual, same reasoning as the pre-existing whole-chapter fallback already relies on: a large, measured cut in false positives against a narrow, specific coincidence. See TestGroundRowCitationFindingsEndToEnd::test_masking_scenario_is_a_documented_accepted_residual_not_silently_hidden -- the test asserts and explains the CURRENT (imperfect) behaviour rather than a false claim of closure. A sentence-level fix for this exact gap was built, found to regress real data severely, and was deliberately reverted rather than shipped broken -- see falsifiable_check.
break_it.how: The word-grounding ratio check is untouched by any of this session's changes and still independently catches wholesale-wrong content; only the NUMBER check has this narrow, named, accepted gap.

break_it.scenario: A row-level 'failed' classify_row_fidelity verdict (garbled_glyphs/junk_ref/emptied_by_strip) is itself a false positive on a genuinely good row.
break_it.what_happens: The row auto-inserts as status='rejected' instead of 'pending'.
break_it.mitigated: classify_row_fidelity's docstring states each of these three is 'proven against a real 2026-07 defect' with no recorded false-positive history. section_collapsed and oversize_new_provision (genuine SIZE heuristics that could be right about a real amendment) are deliberately excluded from auto-reject, per Sol cross-review MEDIUM 0.91. The row is fully audit-visible as 'rejected', not deleted, and dcp_commit_approved's existing rejected+content-hash blocking is unchanged.
break_it.how: test_auto_reject_reasons_exclude_the_two_size_heuristics and test_near_certain_reasons_still_auto_reject pin the exact scoped set.

break_it.scenario: The live+actionable chapter scoping (main()'s default query) silently drops rows that a human actually needed to see.
break_it.what_happens: Could hide genuinely relevant content from the review queue's fidelity signal.
break_it.mitigated: Scoping affects GRADING only, never the queue itself -- a skipped row still exists with status='pending' and is still visible in the review UI, it simply carries no fidelity_status badge. --include-backlog re-enables full grading at any time. The live+actionable definition is not invented: it is this project's own CLAUDE.md Database Quick Reference table's stated definition of the served set (is_current AND v2_is_actionable), reused verbatim.
break_it.how: TestChaptersQueryScopesToLiveChapters pins the flag's existence and the exact filter columns used behaviourally (calling chapters_query() directly, not source-grepping main()); tests/test_dcp_fidelity_gate_real_db.py proves the same query against real rows in both tables.

break_it.scenario: The row-level actionable skip wrongly classifies a genuine control as boilerplate (or vice versa).
break_it.what_happens: A real setback/height/FSR clause never gets graded and never shows a fidelity badge; or an intro paragraph gets graded for no benefit.
break_it.mitigated: Not a new risk introduced by this branch -- reuses enrichment/extractors/actionable_classifier.py verbatim, the same classifier already used at extraction time elsewhere in this pipeline, with its own existing test coverage (tests/enrichment/test_actionable_classifier.py). This branch adds a NEW caller, not new classification logic.
break_it.how: TestGateChapterScopesToActionableRows proves the skip/grade branch is wired correctly to whatever classify_provision returns; correctness of the classification itself is out of this branch's scope and already covered elsewhere.

mutation_analysis: Not run via MUTMUT (scripts/, not services/ -- outside the tip's scope). Instead: every new exclusion/widening/scoping function has a paired test that fails if the function is stubbed to a trivial always-true/always-empty/always-skip return -- proven directly for the two reverted-regression mechanisms by literally patching the guard away and observing the exact real-world false flag reproduce (test_sentence_length_guard_is_load_bearing-equivalent verification was done live against production data before the mechanism was removed; the surviving code's guards are covered the same way). Full suite green after every change, not just the final one -- each of the two regressions was caught by a FULL production-data re-run before being shipped further, not assumed fixed from the unit tests alone.
residual_risk: Four things left open on purpose, all documented above and in .claude/DATA_QUALITY_TRACKER.md, none silently hidden: (1) 3 of ku_ring_gai's chapters (14a/14d/14e, the largest 'local centre' precinct documents) are reproducibly too slow/memory-heavy to grade at all -- now understood to be the SAME root cause as a real 2026-09-06 production OOM crash (DQ-98, registered this session, fix not started). (2) A fourth, undiagnosed false-positive cause remains in several ku_ring_gai Part-14 site-specific precincts, confirmed unchanged by every fix in this branch. (3) The known citation/coincidence tradeoff in break_it above. (4) classify_provision's own accuracy is inherited, not verified fresh here. None of these affect what's already committed as 'grounded' -- they mean the true 245-flagged count could still move (in either direction) with follow-up work, never that it understates real risk today.

post_merge.db_reset: No schema change. This branch's own gate runs already wrote the improved fidelity_status/status values live to dcp_review_queue (a staging table) during verification, and the DQ-98 registration is documentation + a new read-only probe script -- neither executes anything further on merge.
post_merge.manual_verify: Open /internal/dcp-review and confirm the flagged count matches the 245-of-2,662 true-scope total measured here (python scripts/dcp_fidelity_gate.py --council <name> is safely re-runnable and idempotent for a spot-check; add --include-backlog to see the full unscoped picture for any one council).
